adds.title: Public Defender of Amapá - non-binary gender change access
adds.summary: On 19 February 2022 in Amapá the State Public Defender's Office filed its first request for civil-registry name and gender rectification for a non-binary person, affirming such rectification as legally viable as for transgender persons on the basis of self-determination and the registry's function to reflect social presentation; the procedure follows the same process as any civil-registry alteration and the Defender's Office provides assistance for such requests.

adds.title: Macapá City Hall / University Hospital / AMA-LBTI Center - gender-affirming care
adds.summary: On 13 February 2025 Macapá opened its first Municipal Trans Outpatient Clinic at the Papaléo Paes Specialties Center operating Monday to Friday 8h to 17h offering free integral multidisciplinary transition care for trans, travesti and non-binary people with no age restriction including general medicine, nursing, endocrinology, gynecology, dermatology, psychiatry, urology, cardiology, psychology, nutrition, social work, physiotherapy, speech therapy, dentistry, laboratory exams, ultrasound, mammography, densitometry, provision of testosterone cypionate and estradiol per clinical protocol, vaccination, rapid tests, Pap smear collection and dressings with access by UBS referral or walk-in requiring RG, CPF and SUS card with initial general-practitioner evaluation and referral while excluding clinical demands unrelated to gender transition

adds.title: Supreme Federal Court ruling, March 2018 - legal gender change
adds.summary: In March 2018 Brazil's Supreme Federal Court ruled that transgender people can change their legal name and gender marker on civil records by self-identification without requiring surgery, hormonal treatment, or judicial authorization.

adds.title: Manaus municipal law banning unisex restrooms, 18 October 2022
adds.summary: On 18 October 2022, the city of Manaus enacted a municipal law prohibiting multigender/unisex restrooms.
